Brick, mortar and render.

Repointing

Gaps in old mortar let water in. Repointing keeps the walls weatherproof and repairs the structural integrity of the brickwork.

  1. Old mortar outRemoved with angle grinders for clean cuts to the top and bottom joints. Where power tools can’t be used, hand tools such as comb hammers.
  2. Brickwork cleanedCleaned first, so the new mortar has maximum grip.
  3. New mortar inApplied to the prepared joints.
Why repoint?
  • Stops damp getting in through holes and gaps
  • Improves how the property looks
  • Adds value, because well-kept brickwork gives a good first impression
  • Helps saleability: poor mortar is commonly raised on a valuer’s report
